author.name: 松紡雫（まちゅむしじゅく）

details:
Environment

　-OS: Windows 10

　-VR Device: Meta Quest 2 (PCVR)

　-Platform: VRChat (PC)

　-Event: Vket Winter 2025

　-Location: Company Booth Worlds (e.g. Shinjuku Monorail area)

Description

　During Vket Winter 2025, I experienced a VR freeze followed by a forced application exit while visiting company booth worlds.

　This issue appears to be related to newly introduced moving-platform gimmicks (e.g. monorail and escalator systems) that allow players to remain standing, walk, and jump without using a Sit interaction.

　Notably, this behavior does not occur in most user-created worlds, and I was able to reproduce the issue intentionally after the event in order to collect logs.

Observed Behavior

　-The player avatar moves together with the vehicle/platform without Sit constraints

　-The player can walk and jump freely while the platform is moving

　-After some time, the screen freezes and VRChat exits

　-No GPU crash, VRAM error, or OS-level error is observed

Log Information (Key Points)

　-Repeated warnings:

　　Player transform is not aligned with the XZ plane. Correcting!

　-Followed by multiple NullReferenceException errors during shutdown

　-Errors appear mainly during OnDestroy() and cleanup phases

　-No DXGI_ERROR, Device Removed, or Out of Memory messages found

Reproduction Steps

　1. Launch VRChat on Windows 10 using Quest 2 (PCVR)

　2. Enter a Vket Winter 2025 company booth world

　3. Use the new monorail or escalator gimmick

　　　-Remain standing (no Sit)

　　　-Walk and/or jump while the platform is moving

　4. After some time, the player transform becomes unstable and VRChat exits

Analysis / Hypothesis

This issue seems to occur when:

　-The world continuously modifies the player’s transform to synchronize with a moving platform

　-At the same time, player input (movement / jump) and VRChat’s own player correction logic are applied

　-Under performance constraints, frame timing becomes inconsistent

　-This results in transform misalignment (XZ plane correction spam), eventually leading to an unrecoverable state

The problem appears to be world-side transform synchronization, rather than a hardware or OS failure.

Additional Notes

　-I intentionally reproduced the issue after completing the event to verify whether it was caused by my PC or VR device

　-The issue does not commonly occur in non-event or user-created worlds

　-This suggests an edge case involving new moving-platform mechanics under VR conditions
title: VR Freeze / Forced Exit when using new moving-platform gimmicks (Vket Winter 2025 – Company Booth Worlds)
